findings.title: One commit (544e9daa2) fixing an unrelated, pre-existing typecheck defect names no ticket in its subject line
findings.evidence: WORK-ORDER.md rule 2: "One ticket = its own commits, whose messages name it (`fix(web): #896 …`)." Commit 544e9daa2's subject is `fix(web): document-kind-dialog references the renamed DOCUMENT_KINDS export` -- no `#NNN`. The commit body explains at length why (a pre-existing, unrelated defect blocking #934's own required gates, confirmed by git log to predate this lane), and ticket #934's report cross-references it fully, but the literal rule is not followed.
findings.required_fix: No fix required retroactively (the commit is already landed, well-justified and fully traceable via its own body and ticket #934's report). Worth a one-line addendum to WORK-ORDER.md for a future lane: a commit that fixes a cross-cutting, pre-existing defect blocking a ticket's own gates may cite the blocking ticket in its body without a `#NNN` prefix in the subject, as long as it says so as explicitly as this one does.

findings.title: The two-item conditional-required predicate is repeated three times, inline, inside clara.get_firm_setup
findings.evidence: 0257_firm_setup_applicability.sql's recut `clara.get_firm_setup` repeats `k.item_key in ('mpers_eligibility','tin') and ... clara._firm_setup_applicability(p.id, k.item_key) = 'applicable'` three times with small variations: once in the per-item `'required'` field (line ~389), once in `v_req_total` (line ~449) and once in `v_req_done` (line ~456-457) -- a possible Fowler 'Duplicated Code' judgement call.
findings.required_fix: No fix required. The migration's own header ("REGRESSION THIS FILE MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY AVOIDED") explains the `i.id is not null` asymmetry between the three sites, and the migration's tail census string-matches each of the three occurrences independently as a separate assertion -- collapsing them into one shared CTE/lateral expression would make the tail's per-site verification weaker, not stronger, in a house style that otherwise always favours an independently re-measurable tail over a DRY-er body. A documented-standard override, not a violation; noted for calibration only.

summary: All five tickets (#894, #895, #891, #934, #935) comply with the repo's documented migration house shape: header, prestate pins measured live on clara_l06 (sha256(prosrc), pg_get_indexdef, pg_constraint defs, row-hash baselines) rather than transcribed, tail assertions that re-read the committed catalog, redo-safety guards (if not exists / definition probes), a preintegration-gate module with a stable stem for every migration, rig-meta.mjs cohort entries added only where a GRANTED name actually changed (once, for #935's dismiss_firm_setup_tip), and owner/SECURITY DEFINER/search_path/plan_cache_mode/ACL preserved and re-measured on every recut body. No new relation is created anywhere in the diff, so the FORCE RLS / zero-application-role-DML rule is not applicable. No applied migration is edited, no PRD/ARCHITECTURE edit, no frozen-workflow manifest diff (packages/runtime is untouched by this lane). Test quality against /tdd is strong throughout: every DB cell drives the two named doors (or the one new door) through humanQuery as a real persona, expected values are transcribed independently from the ticket/owner-ruling text rather than recomputed from the implementation, no internal collaborator or private function is asserted against, and the web tests mock only the fetch boundary. git log confirms ten genuinely vertical-sliced commits (migration+test, or component+test, together) with no battery of red tests committed ahead of any implementation. Independent verification on the live rig reproduced every load-bearing claim: 35/35 firm-setup DB cells green, 10/10 operation-census, 22/23 rig-isolation (1 correctly-skipped destructive cell), the gate-chain growing by exactly five entries in migration order, and the rig-meta.mjs cohort diff being the single, correctly-scoped addition the reports describe. Two minor/note-level observations are recorded above; neither is a hard violation and neither blocks acceptance.
